Digital, IEC 61850 enabled substation systems can be fully implemented at station and process bus level, which would arguably reduce cost and increase overall efficiency for installation, commissioning, operation, and maintenance. Such complete integration needs careful management to ensure continued reliability of critical systems. National Grid Electricity Transmission Plc has been conservatively playing its role in enabling digital substation solutions for some years. This paper discusses the evolution of various aspects of digital substation technology within transmission networks, presents progression within communication protocols, and highlights some of the milestone projects. It also presents some of the challenges and opportunities that the company is faced with in the digital substation context.

articleTitle: Witness the digital transformation in Taiwan's protection system from 2017 to 2021
publicationTitle: 16th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2022)
abstract: After the blackout in Taipei on 15 Aug 2017, Taiwan Power Company (TPC) rolled out the urgent plan to upgrade the power system protection automation and control with IEC 61850. The major upgrade is focused on the protection relay information flow and time synchronisation. In order to ensure the implementation at the highest quality and speed, TPC management and engineers adapted a list of quality control actions at different stages of their implementation. Our IEC 61850 consulting team reinforced TPC since the very first session and witnessed the whole digital transformation process from 2017 to the present. This paper will share TPC's approach in adapting the general interoperability test from UCAiug's IOP session. We will also share the unique test requirement because of the localised need for IEC61850 digitalisation. Our paper will also share the importance of education and suggest the most effective IEC 61850 training based on the level of demand in Taiwan.

articleTitle: A sensitive line differential protection solution for high impedance fault detection
publicationTitle: 16th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2022)
abstract: This paper proposes a sensitive line differential protection solution utilizing dedicated measurements which are based on zero-sequence current differential signal detection with multi-terminal measurement inputs. The advantage of using zero-sequence current line differential is obvious due to the clear selectivity and sensitivity. Further, with the use of zero-sequence measurements, the scheme performance is not affected by the presence of the charging current. The proposed function also includes an integrated fast phase selection solution so that the function is suitable for applications where selective single-pole tripping/auto reclosing is required. In addition to the above features, a three stage of sensitive zero-sequence differential current protection has been arranged to handle the impact of possible asymmetrical switching such as circuit breaker operations in one end of the protected line and shunt reactor operations in the line so that fast speed and good security of protection solution could be achieved at the same time.

articleTitle: System integrity protection by orbital grid-forming mode for VSC
publicationTitle: 16th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2022)
abstract: The primary challenge is to develop a protective function that utilises a VSC for fulfilling this task of dynamic system stabilization. In consequence, the protection function is realized in form of a converter control scheme that enables the VSC's operation in grid-forming mode (OGM) alongside with the synchronous generator. The Orbital Grid-forming mode OGM offers current limitation without a separate control-loop and even without measuring the current. Furthermore, it enables the VSC to stabilize electromechanical dynamics of synchronous machines by obtaining a maximum angular deviation between its internal voltage and their rotors. This means a generator cannot lose synchronism to the VSC and its rotor experiences a floating anchor-point, which hinders its acceleration or deceleration until the dynamic excursion of the machine is over.

articleTitle: Three-phase power transformer protection, automation and control specification using IEC 61850 system configuration description language
publicationTitle: 16th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2022)
abstract: The paper presents the Protection, Automation and Control System specification for a digital substation conceived using the IEC 61850 System Configuration description Language for a three-phase power transformer applied on electrical energy transmission systems. The specification includes power transformer supervision data, fan, and Load Tap Changer (LTC) control and protection functions design for a digital substation with process bus application. Two concepts were adopted on the System Specification Description (SSD) file development. The former application considers the digitalization made with Process Interface Units among the bays and the power transformer. The latter assumes digital primary equipment on the substation, where each equipment has its own digital controller. Details about the SSD file's substation, communication and IED parts are described. To validate the proposed design, the LTC control was configured on commercial IEDs to simulate three power transformers parallel operation on a test bench. The results showed the feasibility to apply the LTC control design on commercial IEDs and the developments needed to proper use the SSD file on a top-down configuration approach.

articleTitle: Optimal overcurrent relay coordination based on hybrid water cycle moth flame optimization (HWCMFO) algorithm considering standard and non-standard characteristics of microgrids
publicationTitle: 16th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2022)
abstract: Due to the ever-increasing participation of Distributed Generation (DG) and the multi-looped structure of modern distribution networks (DNs), the optimal coordination and reduction of the tripping time of Overcurrent Relays (OCRs) have recently become a significant challenge. In addition, the variable Microgrids (MGs) operational modes have raised the computational burden and complexity to acquire the OCRs optimal settings. In this context, obtaining a reliable performance of MGs in both grid-connected and islanding operational modes requires non-classical approaches to solve OCRs coordination issues. This study investigates the impact of immoderate fault current owing to the presence of DG on traditional IEC characteristics. A non-standards approach has been proposed for optimal coordination of OCRs in MGs by extending the IEC normal inverse characteristics to fifty Plug Setting Multiplier (PSM. An artificial intelligence hybrid algorithm based on Water Cycle Moth Flame Optimization (HWCMFO) has been used as an optimization technique in OCRs coordination protection to optimize the maximum PSM limits. Several scenarios have been implemented and tested with an IEC MG benchmark. The obtained results have illustrated the effectiveness and applicability of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Attack tree analysis of a digital secondary system in an electrical substation
publicationTitle: 16th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2022)
abstract: Modern digital secondary system (DSS) technology uses digital communications among relays and remote digital sensors over high-speed fiber connections to perform fault detection and trip circuit control. A cyber vulnerability assessment of each proposed communications design is essential to evaluate the energy control system's reliability. Many cybersecurity technologies from numerous industries are promoted for use in DSS communications with unknown impacts. This paper introduces appropriate metrics and a cyber vulnerability assessment framework, using the attack tree method, to compare the cyber risk of available technologies to determine the dependability and security of digital control and protective trip circuits.

articleTitle: Effects of lightning strikes to the travelling wave fault location system of a transmission line
publicationTitle: 16th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2022)
abstract: Lightning strikes on an electric power transmission system can be categorised into induced strikes, back strikes and direct strikes. Waveform recognition techniques are now available to categorise such events based on the travelling wave signals captured. This paper explains the travelling wave characteristics of different types of lightning strikes based on which waveform recognition can be applied to categorise the events. Modern travelling wave fault location system (TWFL) is able to provide automatic event categorisation. It also provides both double-ended and single-ended fault location. Double-ended fault location relies on data acquisition units at both ends of the line to capture the arrival times of the first travelling waves to calculate the fault location automatically. Single-ended method relies the time difference between the incident and the reflected waves at one end to calculate the fault location. Analysis of the site records has shown that the lightning strike position and the fault position may not be the same. This is because the overvoltage can cause insulation breakdown at the weakest point along the line, which may not coincide with the strike point. This discrepancy cannot be resolved by the double-ended method, but the single-ended method can effectively identify the actual fault location.

articleTitle: A transmission utility's experience – asset replacement of static low impedance biased differential busbar protection systems
publicationTitle: 16th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2022)
abstract:
National Grid Electricity Transmission (NGET) has a number of Static Low Impedance Biased Differential Busbar Protection Systems installed around 1988 and 2001, all are still in operational service on double busbar substations operating at 132kV and below. This paper considers the drivers, options, and complexities for their asset replacement.

))Operational experience and asset performance to date - Busbar protection needs to be secure / stable and free from un-necessary operation during faults outside of the busbar zone of protection (through faults). Also, it needs to be dependable and able to detect an in-zone busbar fault quickly (<40ms) to be able to limit widespread system disturbance.))

))Challenges on supporting legacy systems, obsolesce, spares and extension - Post commissioning, the protection systems need lifetime operational support. This will include fault identification and repair, routine maintenance, spares management, obsolesce issues and substation modification requirements. This paper will consider these challenges during the different phases of the asset lifecycle.))

))Options considered for asset replacement – Asset replacement of a busbar protection system on a live double busbar substation presents multiple challenges. Many factors impact on this including – the design of the existing system, the design and technology of the proposed replacement system, available system access and outages during the replacement works, protecting the substation busbars during the replacement work and limitations around plant interfaces and physical space constraints.))

))Chosen technology, replacement methodology options and progress to date - This paper will look at progress to date on this asset replacement work, the system architecture and technology chosen and will also consider strategies to replace the whole NGET population of this protection type))

articleTitle: A dependable and secure adaptive distance protection scheme against resistive faults
publicationTitle: 16th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2022)
abstract: Distance relays with set trip boundaries are prone to failure against resistive faults. This is because the apparent impedance may deviate significantly from the impedance of the faulted line segment. Adaptive distance relaying is a viable solution for this problem, which may include either changing the trip characteristics of the relay or modifying the apparent impedance calculation to compensate for the deviation. While the former approach may compromise relay selectivity, the latter typically assumes structural characteristics such as system homogeneity, which may not always be applicable. In this paper, we propose a scheme for adapting the zone-1 operation of a distance relay for transmission lines. The scheme combines merits of both the approaches discussed earlier. This means, to improve dependability, it utilizes the adapted relay characteristics corresponding to the prevalent system operating condition. In addition, to maintain relay security, an internal adaptive check is deployed on the measured apparent impedance to ensure that it is not an out-of-zone fault. This step produces an estimate of a “compensated” apparent impedance which determines fault within or out of zone with respect to the base (fixed) zone-1 boundaries. The proposed scheme is illustrated by case studies on the IEEE 39 bus test system.

articleTitle: Compensation of impedance measurement error due to arcing
publicationTitle: 16th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2022)
abstract: Arcing is a phenomenon which is closely related to short circuits in electrical systems. The nature of arcing can be different but, in any case, there is no universal mathematical model to describe arcing. In a general approach arcing is described with a non-linear, but only resistive voltage-current characteristic. Based on this assumption the distance protection is using the R-reach of the characteristic to cover the arc impedance. For the impedance-based fault location a similar approach applies. If the arc is only resistive, the reactance measurement used for the fault location is not influenced. This paper presents two real cases where impedance measurement errors due to arcing can heavily influence the behaviour of distance protection and impedance-based fault location. In the first example the fault locator estimates a location with an unacceptable measurement error. This happens after a successful trip of the line differential protection on a 400kV line with single side infeed only. The arcing impacts the voltage measurement in magnitude and phase angle which finally leads to the incorrect estimation of the fault location. The second example is about distance protection applied to a medium voltage cable. Due to the arcing a fault in zone 1 is measured to be outside of zone 1 for a long time. After approximately 170 ms the characteristic of the arc is changing which enables the distance protection to measure the fault in zone 1 and send a trip command to clear the fault. The paper analyses the two cases in detail and suggests a method how to improve the impedance measurement for distance protection and fault location in such cases of arcing.

articleTitle: Simulation on single-pole tripping of phase segregated current differential relay protection for six-phase feeder in digsilent powerfactory
publicationTitle: 16th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2022)
abstract: Converting an existing double-circuit three-phase (3Φ) line into a single six-phase (6Φ) transmission feeder operating at a higher phase-to-ground voltage increases the power transfer capability. The use of 6Φ transmission complicates possible short-circuit fault conditions and the number of significant fault types increases to 23, with 120 possible different combinations. The impact on system stability of tripping the entire feeder may be unacceptable, and consequently single pole tripping is required. This paper investigates the suitability of applying a phase segregated current differential protection scheme with single-pole tripping to a simplified 6Φ network, modelled in DIgSILENT PowerFactory®. The conventional 3Φ tripping logic was modified to ensure the correct single-pole tripping results were obtained for all fault types.

articleTitle: A novel protection principle for ultra-high-speed tripping of lines terminated on transformers
publicationTitle: 16th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2022)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel protection principle for lines connected to the bulk power system at one end (system terminal) and terminated exclusively on power transformers or current-limiting reactors at the other end (transformer terminal). The new protection principle operates as fast as 1 to 2 ms and covers the entire line length without the need for a protection channel. The new principle is based on the current traveling-wave magnitude measured at the system terminal of the line.

articleTitle: Adaptive protection of microgrid through abrupt change analysis and fractional fourier transform
publicationTitle: 16th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2022)
abstract: This paper presents wavelet and fractional fourier transform based adaptive protection in low X/R microgrid architecture to analyse fault coefficients through wavelet analysis and fractional fourier transform under islanded and grid connected modes of operation. This approach can be extended for island detection and fault nature classification during different modes of microgrid operation. Its efficacy in the real time scenario is tested under the shunt faults during different modes of microgrid operation. Different phase faults, and earth faults are simulated both in islanded and grid connected modes using Matlab/Simulink software. The waveforms wavelet coefficients of fault current in I<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">q</sub> attributes in each mode are detected based on fractional fourier transform. The proposed adaptive protection technique reduces the separate analysis of transients for real time applications and is found out to be more accurate and robust in comparison to other approaches. The simulation results reveal that there are specific distinguishable changes in the fault current contribution for different types of faults in microgrid operation. Accordingly, intelligent adaptive protection scheme is proposed for fault detection, and island detection to ensure secure and reliable performance of protective relay for microgrid structures.

articleTitle: A least square regression based fault locator for unbalanced faults on a transmission line
publicationTitle: 16th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2022)
abstract: Associated with the sequence analysis of voltage measurement at one end of a transmission line, least square regression (LSR) is applied to determine the fault locations of this line under unbalanced faults in a non-radial wind power integrated electrical grid. Under this approach, the data-driven models illustrating fault characteristics are built in MATLAB/Simulink, so the fault locations can be accurately estimated for the facilitation of relevant protection schemes in real time. The effectiveness of LSR estimating fault locations is validated through a stochastic Monte Carlo simulation (MCS) with the involvement of noise.

articleTitle: Functional digital twins of relay protection and relay test equipment enabling benefits in training and remote support
publicationTitle: 16th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2022)
abstract: Simulating functional performance in a computer - a digital twin - delivers benefits that include reduced costs, increased reliability, and better efficiency. Two of the major application areas for this new technology applied to protection relays are training and remote support. In this paper we will focus on what has been achieved today in these two topics with an insight into future possibilities. From a training perspective, a digital twin of protection relays and a relay test sets can greatly increase accessibility to all technicians and engineers. It will provide a means to get hands on experience and greatly reduce the cost. This will provide opportunity to many more employees instead of a chosen few due to the complexity of resources that are necessary when performing these types of training. Form a remote support perspective, enable the possibility to replicate a remote customer setup which can be used for troubleshooting and give expertise guidance of how to proceed to the engineers that need help in the substation. The virtual tests can be performed at home during normal work hours and the support specialist can provide a validated solution which the test engineer can repeat independently during their own work hours. In both these applications it is of fundamental importance that the twins can share the same data. This paper will detail on this important concept as well.

articleTitle: Testing & commissioning of digital substation - IEC 61850-9-2 LE complied IEDs & merging units
publicationTitle: 16th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2022)
abstract: Power system protection has undergone a huge revolution in the recent times owing to the advancements happening in the communication technology and the standards defined by international committees. One such standard defined by IEC61850 has been under extensive implementation in many parts of the world. The standard has segregated the implementation methods in chapter 8-1 for digital information transfer and chapter 9-2 for analog information transfer between the protection, control and switchgear equipment. This has led to reduction and elimination of copper cable in the substation which has been in the form of panel wiring, inter panel wiring and cables between switchyard to control room. The panel wiring was minimized by the use of advance features available in numerical relays, and the inter panel wiring has been diminished by the use of relay to relay communication defined as generic object-oriented substation event (GOOSE) in IEC61850-8-1. Further, the copper cable elimination was also defined in IEC61850-9-2 by use of equipment such as merging units and optical current / voltage transformers. This equipment provides the option for the user to eliminate huge cost due to reduction of copper cables, and compact solution with minimum equipment without compromising the quality delivered. Such a substation would be categorized as digital substation [1] and the high-end communication gateway would further provide the user the option to run the substation from remote (Unmanned substations) On the other hand, the implementation of such a system throws challenges to the users when products from various vendors are integrated and is to be tested in accordance to the specification and that of the standard. This challenge is addressed to a certain extent by the light edition of IEC61850-9-2 defined as IEC61850-9-2LE [2]. In accordance to this standard, the major components such as intelligent electronic devise, merging unit, optical / conventional current and voltage transformers, ethernet switch, time synchronization equipment etc.. has to be tested and commissioned. The step by step testing methodology involved in testing of the major components of digital substation in accordance to IEC61850-9-2LE standard is the attempt and scope of this paper.

articleTitle: A comprehensive review of the protection methods applied to the MTDC systems
publicationTitle: 16th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2022)
abstract: With the recent development in voltage source converters (VSC), modular multi-level converter (MMC) topology has been recognised as the most suitable topology for building multi-terminal direct current (MTDC) grids. Today, several MMC-based MTDC projects have been commissioned. The primary motivation to construct such advanced MTDC grids is to ensure the reliable and economical operation of the interconnected power system. Protection of MTDC grids is a vital task, requiring effective protection algorithms to detect the transients in milliseconds and isolate the healthy and unhealthy parts quickly. The emerging technology of hybrid direct current circuit breakers (DCCBs) assures the deenergization of the faulty section in an MTDC system. However, such a solution is uneconomical and produces increased power losses. This research work provides a comprehensive review of different protection devices and fault detection methods for MTDC systems. In addition, the effects of measuring and communication devices on protection methods are also discussed. Finally, the challenges for existing protection systems are discussed and some future recommendations are presented.
